video.title: How To Get Paid $2,500 + Monthly Checks for "Drag & Drop" AI Employees

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Danny, a member of his TK Owners community, who builds AI voice agents (on Go High Level) for local businesses such as barbers. He built a free missed-call voice agent and website for his own barber, which produced a referral chain and several inbound calls from barbers. Danny plans to charge $2,500-$5,000 upfront plus $200-$500 per month. His sales method is to build a Replit website mockup or a live voice agent demo before the first meeting, then reconnect a week or two later to close. The takeaway is to start with a free, high-quality build for someone in your circle and use the result as a showcase and referral source.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: AI voice agent (missed-call answering) for barbers and appointment-based local businesses
ideas.one_liner: Replace a busy barber's voicemail with a Go High Level voice agent that answers questions and texts a booking link, sold with a website and KPI dashboard.
ideas.business_model: Upfront setup fee plus monthly maintenance retainer
ideas.customer: Busy solo barbers and other appointment-based local businesses (salons, nails, massage), often in salon suites; also home inspection, remodeling and other local firms
ideas.problem: Barbers cutting hair cannot answer calls and miss new-customer bookings; voicemail loses leads
ideas.offer: A voice agent trained on the business's website or Google Business Profile that picks up when the owner does not answer, answers FAQs and opening hours, and texts the booking link. Bundled with a new website, KPI dashboard, SMS marketing, newsletters and reactivation tools.

pricing.model: Upfront setup fee plus monthly fee, customised per client

price_points.label: range of willingness to pay from other prospects

pricing.notes: Danny says the range depends on the client's understanding of the value and their stage; he avoids charging startups with no money. His first barber got it free in exchange for being a test case and referral source.

acquisition_channels.details: Free build for his own barber produced a referral from a medical-practice client in the same salon suite building, plus four or five calls in a week from barbers introduced by that one free customer. No ad or sponsorship spend.

quote.text: I haven't spent anything on ads. I haven't spent anything on on sponsorships or anything like that.
quote.speaker: Danny

acquisition_channels.details: Walk into barber shops, ask if they have heard of voice agents, and demo live by calling the number while they cut hair. Chris suggests changing the business name in the agent on your phone to the prospect's name and calling them. Also demoed to neighbouring salon staff in the shared building.
Danny found his tools and training through Koerner's TK Owners community. Sphere of influence (own barber, oil-change person, family) is the starting point.
Pre-built Replit website mockup made before the first meeting, after researching the prospect's current site with ChatGPT; reconnect in a week or two to close.

ideas.delivery: Danny does sales and vision; a coding-capable business partner handles integrations and fixes. The voice agent is set up in Go High Level by linking the website or Google Business Profile, connected to the client's work number so it answers when the owner does not pick up (rings first, then the agent). Replit builds the website and KPI dashboard. Danny says setup takes just a few clicks.
unit_economics_claims: $2,500 to $5,000 upfront plus $200 to $500 per month
Goal of 20 clients as passive income
First barber would pay about $2,500 upfront and $200 a month
125 missed calls handled on the test account since the number was created
ideas.startup_cost: Low; the first build was done for free on a Go High Level account supplied by Koerner. Ongoing Go High Level cost not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; first customer was free, paid pricing is still being set

acquisition.how: The main acquisition is in-person demos at shops and referrals. Inbound content or ads could be automated, but cold DMs to sole traders would breach PECR, so little of the described method is automatable.

onboarding.how: Agent can be trained from a website or Google profile with a few clicks; an agent could gather business info, but number porting and call-forwarding setup need some human checks.

delivery.how: Once configured the voice agent handles calls and texts links unattended; builds of sites and dashboards are agent-assisted but need occasional human fixes.

billing.how: Go High Level supports subscriptions and invoicing; the setup invoice is simple.

support.how: Agent transcripts allow monitoring; clients still need occasional script or knowledge updates and human handling of complaints.

uk_applicability.notes: The model works in the UK, since barbers, salons and UK telephony numbers can be linked to Go High Level. Changes needed: UK call recording/AI disclosure and GDPR consent for transcripts, UK number forwarding, GBP pricing, and the agent should disclose that it is an AI to be safe. Cold outreach to sole traders is restricted by PECR, so in-person selling or inbound is safer.

risks: Windows of opportunity close as competition and easier tools arrive
Low ticket size per barber limits revenue per client
Agent in the demo posed as a human; it may need to disclose it is AI
Reliance on Go High Level pricing and reseller terms
Medical or higher-stakes practices need human handoff
Replit builds can stall and need a coder to finish

tactics.name: Free first client as test case and referral engine
steps: Pick a well-connected local business owner in your circle, ideally in a shared building with many other businesses
Build the website and voice agent for free and say upfront it is a test
Ask what they would pay to gauge pricing
Let them demo it to neighbours and refer you

quote.text: you're my lead magnet. Not only do you have 20 other businesses in here
quote.speaker: Danny

tactics.name: Build before the meeting
steps: Research prospect's current website with ChatGPT for flaws
Create a Replit mockup before the first meeting and show it via link
Hold a roughly one-hour discovery conversation about goals and year plans
Build something to show and reconnect in a week or two to close

quote.text: just showing your potential and they're like man this is amazing it looks good.
quote.speaker: Danny

tactics.name: Live voice agent demo while getting a haircut
steps: Set up the agent on your phone with the prospect's business name and website
Call the shop's number while they cut your hair and have them talk to it
Close the sale with the demo

quote.text: you open up high level on your phone and you go to the settings for the voice agent and you change out the name of the business to his business name
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Ring-then-agent call routing
steps: Connect the owner's work number to Go High Level
Let it ring a few times so the owner can answer
If unanswered, route to the voice agent instead of voicemail
Agent texts the booking link to the caller

tactics.name: Add KPI dashboard and fear metrics
steps: Build a dashboard in Replit with metrics relevant to the business
Show potential lost revenue from unbooked days
Use ChatGPT to suggest actions like targeted days or texts

lessons.lesson: Start with a free, excellent build for someone in your sphere; if it is magical you get referrals or paid work, if not you learn.

quote.text: either you win or you learn, right?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Showing finished work before the sale makes value visible and triggers reciprocity and confirmation bias, while reducing post-sale work.
Solve current, concrete problems for existing businesses instead of inventing new products.

quote.text: figure out what people's current problems are and and go that route
quote.speaker: Danny

lessons.lesson: AI makes agency services viable for solo businesses that could never afford agencies, trading ticket size for numbers.
Pair a sales-focused founder with a technical partner to cover the last mile of builds.
Do not wait to learn everything before starting; get hands dirty.

quote.text: the idea that you need to learn every single thing before you start is absurd.
quote.speaker: Danny

lessons.lesson: A long discovery conversation about the owner's goals reveals problems they cannot name themselves.
Opportunity windows (Yelp, PPC, voice agents) are short but later entrants still succeed.

evidence_quality.rationale: Danny is a first-hand operator, but he has only one free client and no paid customers yet; prices are targets, and metrics are vague (one dashboard figure of 125 missed calls). The story is real but early and the pricing is aspirational.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes Go High Level via an affiliate link and sells TK Owners and Playmakers communities, from which Danny comes.
